If you observe any unexpected `HTTP 403` responses from a known legitimate service or workflow following the window, please raise it in <#C081Q3TU1UG> immediately.  If you need support or have questions, don't hesitate to reach out. text: __:loudspeaker: Action needed: all **Ingress-using **charts must move to helm-common 1.8.1__  Hi all — we're standardizing on helm-common 1.8.1, and this announcement covers the charts that use Ingress objects.  Why this is needed: we're retiring ingress-nginx, which is now EOL and poses a security risk. SMP customers have expressed great concern and escalated for us to move away from this risk. We're moving to envoy-gateway via the Kubernetes Gateway API, and helm-common 1.8.1 is what adds the support needed for that migration. To get off ingress-nginx cleanly, every ingress-using chart needs to be on 1.8.1.  :dart: Target: we want to go to prod the week of the 20th. To hit that, please land your upgrade by the deadline for your group below.  :date: Timeline  Group 1 → by Monday (Jul 13) Group 2 → by Wednesday (Jul 15) Group 3 → by Friday (Jul 17) Prod rollout → week of Jul 20  Please find your service below and follow the guidance for your group — the effort depends on the version you're on today.  :large_green_circle: Group 1 — On 1.7.2, or already on 1.8.0: quick build (due Mon Jul 13)  You're already close. A quick rebuild of your service should pick up helm-common 1.8.1 — no chart changes expected. author: Jonathan Mell
text: For the record -- i've added kyverno policies in `qa-private` that will prevent pods from starting that require `/var/dumps` and have ENV variable `JFR_DUMP_ROOT_LOCATION` . These will continue to be `Pending` until the JVM-collector pods annotate the node. Everything appears to be working as expected but this is just a heads up in case anybody sees their pods not scheduling.  In most circumstances this race condition of `jvm-collector` not running and pods needing `/var/dumps` only happens on a scaling event.  For whatever reason the last 3 years this has never occurred in production. (Which i think is some kind of miracle)

author: Vineeth Chandran (pronouns: He/Him)
text: **Action Required: ESR Ticket Required for Cloud Engineering Requests**  Hey everyone,  A quick request regarding operational/support issues being raised to the Cloud Engineering team.  We have noticed that a large number of requests/issues are being directly raised in <#C05FG6YL74H> by tagging the Cloud Engineering handle/team members. While the channel can continue to be used for visibility, coordination, or urgent discussions, we need to ensure that all actionable items are backed by an ESR ticket.  Going forward, for any issue/request requiring investigation, operational work, troubleshooting, infra changes, or follow-up from the Cloud Engineering team, please create an ESR ticket first and include the ticket reference in the Slack thread/message.  Without an ESR ticket:  * We will not have proper tracking/prioritization * Ownership and SLA become unclear * Work can get missed during handoffs/shifts * It becomes difficult to manage and prioritize incoming operational load  **Process going forward:**  1. Create an ESR ticket with all relevant details 1. Share the ESR link in Share the ESR link in <#C05FG6YL74H> if visibility/support/escalation is required 1. Cloud Engineering team will use the ESR as the source of truth for tracking and execution  This will help us ensure better prioritization, visibility, accountability, and turnaround for everyone involved.  Thanks for the support and understanding.

author: Jonathan Mell
text: Question for everyone:  It seems with the addition of envoy-gateway as our primary ingress we've run into an issue of HTTP1.1 not being the default.  Once traffic passes identity gateway (gateway pod) H2C is automatically turned on.  At this point if we keep it this way -- Everyone will need to add the following to each of their routes   ```     objects:       - name: <yourroute>         gatewayAPI:           backendTraffic:             useClientProtocol: false ### this is how to disable it.         paths:           - path: /abcd/(123|456) ``` I think this may be painful and annoying so my question is,  Am I correct? Is this painful and annoying? Would you like me to make this the default setting and we can opt into H2C? text: Hello <!S08Q66LS9SL> Does the mongo-query pipeline support javascript queries like the below?  ``` // 1. Define the target URLs const ingressUrl = "<https://harness-ingress-controller>"; const envoyUrl = "<https://envoy-gateway-proxy-envoy-gateway>";  // 2. Initialize an array to hold our bulk update operations const bulkOps = [];  // 3. Find all documents that currently use the ingress URL const ingressDocs = db.getCollection("user_refs").find({ clusterUrl: ingressUrl }).toArray();  print(`Found ${ingressDocs.length} total documents with the ingress URL. Checking for envoy duplicates...`);  // 4. Iterate through each document ingressDocs.forEach(doc => {     // Check if an envoy document already exists for this exact user (by email)     const hasEnvoy = db.getCollection("user_refs").countDocuments({         email: doc.email,         clusterUrl: envoyUrl     });      // 5. If they don't have the envoy document, prepare to update THIS specific document     if (hasEnvoy === 0) {         bulkOps.push({             updateOne: {                 filter: { _id: doc._id },                 update: { $set: { clusterUrl: envoyUrl } }             }         });     } });  // 6. Execute the bulk write if there are documents to update if (bulkOps.length > 0) {     print(`Executing bulk update for ${bulkOps.length} users...`);     const result = db.getCollection("user_refs").bulkWrite(bulkOps);     print(`Success! Updated ${result.modifiedCount} documents to use the envoy URL.`); } else {     print("No updates needed. All users with the ingress URL already have a corresponding envoy document."); } ```

text: Hey <!S08Q66LS9SL>-- the DOPS team needs two Harness delegates provisioned for MongoDB access. PROD0+4 were migrated from Atlas to self-hosted Percona on GKE, and the Atlas clusters were paused on Feb 25, breaking our data pipelines. Per the [Pod Endpoint info doc](https://harness.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEV/pages/23330291751/Self-hosted+MongoDB+Pod+Endpoint+info), these clusters use `*.harness.svc.cluster.local` endpoints (not the *.<http://mongodb.harness.io> ILBs that prod1/2/3 have), so they're only reachable from within their own GKE cluster. No (known to me) existing delegate can reach them. We need a delegate deployed for each row in the table, below. Delegates ultimately need to reach the local Percona MongoDB pods (port 27017) and be selectable by our CI pipelines in PROD org / Data_Ops project.  **Cluster**   **GKE_ID**   PROD0   gke_prod-prod0-3966_us-west1_prod0   PROD4   gke_prod-prod4-2c8f_us-west1_prod4

author: Lijo Jacob
text: Hi <@U07D6DAUXTM>, We got the below request from Disney for Early Release Notifications Before Prod Deployment. Can this be done as a feature request? cc: <@U06BMSLKA85> <@U03RJ200WJX>  ``` Currently, release notes and RSS feed updates are often published after a release has already been deployed to Prod1. For customers who rely on release notes as an early warning system, this timing limits their ability to prepare for UI changes, behavioral updates, or regressions.   When changes reach production before documentation is available, it creates operational risk for large enterprises that need to proactively communicate with internal stakeholders.   Requested Enhancement: Leverage the existing Harness custom banner functionality to provide advance release notifications at least 24 to 48 hours before a release is deployed to production.    Suggested Capabilities:   1. Publish release notes and RSS updates before Prod1 deployment 2. Provide a pre-release notification banner within the Harness UI 3. Offer an opt-in early notification subscription for upcoming releases 4. Include high-level summaries of UI changes, API changes, and behavioral updates     This will give Enterprise customers time to notify internal teams of upcoming changes, validate automation or workflows that could be affected, prepare support teams for potential questions, and review UI changes before they impact end users.   Advance notification would reduce friction during releases and help customers manage stakeholder expectations more effectively. ```

author: Amit Singh
text: Hey <@U07D6DAUXTM> **Need support  to extend `sanity.yaml` to Support Webhook Request Bodies [link](https://harness0.harness.io/ng/account/l7B_kbSEQD2wjrM7PShm5w/module/code/repos/harness-pl-infra/files/refs/heads/master/~/system/environments/sanity/prod/sanity.yaml)**  **Why this matters** Currently, multiple platform services (Access Control, Access Management, etc.) all point to the **same single sanity pipeline** (`platformindividualservicesanity`). Without request body support, the QPE team would need to maintain a separate webhook trigger per service — which means more triggers to manage, more config sprawl, and higher maintenance overhead. With `webhook_body` support in `sanity.yaml`:  * **One webhook URL, many services** — All platform services can share the same `testingservicesanitytrigger` endpoint; the `moduleList` in the request body tells the pipeline which service/stage to run * **QPE team no longer needs to maintain multiple webhooks** for the same pipeline — just one trigger, differentiated by payload * **Cleaner config** — Adding a new platform service means adding one entry in `sanity.yaml` with a body, not creating a new Harness trigger * **Scales easily** — As more services onboard to `platformindividualservicesanity`, they just register themselves with the right `moduleList` value  **Context** Platform services use `platformindividualservicesanity` with `testingservicesanitytrigger`, which requires a custom `moduleList` in the request body to select which stage runs. Without body support in `sanity.yaml`, these triggers cannot be driven from the config today. **What needs to be done** 1.  Change — add optional `webhook_body` field to `sanity.yaml`  ``` services:   access-control:     webhook_url: "<https://harness0.harness.io/gateway/pipeline/api/webhook/custom/rAjjWflwQz2otsJmQqmnNw/v3?accountIdentifier=l7B_kbSEQD2wjrM7PShm5w&orgIdentifier=PROD&projectIdentifier=Quality_Engineering&pipelineIdentifier=platformindividualservicesanity…

author: Mohit Agarwal
text: <!S08Q66LS9SL> Need urgent help. Can you help me with the following:  The Debezium connector for `component-harness.componentsMetadata` has been crash-looping since ~April 16 due to a stale resume token. The connector restarts every ~30 seconds and immediately fails with `ChangeStreamHistoryLost` (Error 286). No CDC events have flowed for this collection in ~a month.  What needs to happen: Connect to the prod-0 Redis instance and delete two keys: `DEBEZIUM_OFFSETS_component-component-harness.componentsMetadata` and `DEBEZIUM_OFFSETS_component-component-harness.componentsMetadata_V2`  Note: Redisson may prefix keys with codec markers. If the exact names don't match, use the `KEYS` output to identify and delete the right ones.  Why both keys: The automated offset reset in debezium-service only clears V1, but `RedisOffsetBackingStore` reads from V2 first. Both must be cleared for a full reset.  What happens after: No pod restart needed. The connector crash-loops every ~30s, so on its next cycle it will find no stored offset, start from the current oplog position, and resume streaming normally. You can verify by watching for `"Handling batch"` logs from debezium-service for `component-harness.componentsMetadata`.  Blast radius: Only affects the `component-harness.componentsMetadata` connector. All other Debezium connectors are unaffected.

author: Manjunatha EN
text: Hi <!S08Q66LS9SL> I’m currently wrapping up the synthetic monitoring setup where we're capturing page load metrics across our different envs. The data is being pushed to InfluxDB, and the goal is to get this all aggregated onto our internal Grafana (`<http://monitoring.harness.io>`) so we can track load times globally. Since the tests are running on **Harness Cloud infra**, I need a hand with the "last mile" of the plumbing:  * **Network Access:** What’s our standard for letting Harness Cloud runners talk to our internal InfluxDB? Should I just provide the Egress CIDRs for allowlisting in the VPC, or do we have an internal proxy/gateway I should be routing through? * **Grafana Integration:** I need to add this Influx as a data source on `<http://monitoring.harness.io>`. Do we manage this via a specific Terraform repo or is there a standard process for onboarding new Influx buckets to the global Grafana? * **Tagging Schema:** To make sure the "all envs" filtering actually works in Grafana, do we have a specific tagging convention I should stick to when pushing the data? (e.g., `harness_env`, `env_type`, `cluster_id`). I want to make sure it aligns with how we already slice and dice metrics elsewhere. cc : <@UDQAS9J5C>

author: Sergey Bobrov
text: <!S03S53DM6TW> Hi team,  :books: Introducing [platform-arch-vault](https://harness0.harness.io/ng/account/l7B_kbSEQD2wjrM7PShm5w/module/code/orgs/PROD/projects/Harness_Commons/repos/platform-arch-vault) — our Harness platform architecture knowledge base  ▎ :warning: Disclaimer: this is ongoing, work-in-progress. Coverage is uneven and some pages lag reality — treat it as a strong starting point.  A knowledge base capturing how our prod cells actually work: gateway/cell/DNS topology, per-cell config drift, and increasingly the platform IAM internals (SSO/SAML/OIDC/SCIM, RBAC, IP allowlists, mTLS, etc.).  Two things live here:  *  Discoverable facts (topology, inventories, config) — generated by scripts in scripts/, dumped to .raw/, ingested into wiki/. The git diff between snapshots is the drift log. *  Narrative knowledge — how a feature works / why a decision was made, written as pages with provenance back to code, Confluence, or live checks.  **How to use it **— point Claude Code/Cursor at the repo and just ask:  * "how does SAML login work for cell X" * "which cells still ride the legacy agent-gateway" * "what's different about eu1's gateway".  It reads the vault, cites the exact pages, and can update them when something's changed. This is the main way in.   Live checks too: it doesn't just read stored snapshots — Claude can run read-only gcloud/kubectl/aws against the right cell (mappings are in scripts/clusters.json) to verify the vault against what's actually deployed, or refresh a discovery  script. Needs VPN + cloud auth.   Prefer to browse visually? Open the folder in Obsidian and explore the graph: wiki/hot.md (recent context) → wiki/index.md (full catalog) → drill via [[wikilinks]]. Good entry points:  * Cell Comparison Matrix * Prod Cell Topology * the IAM Domain index.  Find something new? Extend a discovery script (facts) or add a page (narrative) — conventions are in CLAUDE.md.  cc: <@U01S8B29PFD> <@U0A923GQB9D>
